issues.legal_issue: A suit by a trustee to recover income alleged to be held for a charitable endowment is maintainable where no ground of non-maintainability is demonstrated.
material_facts: The deity, represented by its sole trustee, sued to recover arrears of income and obtain a direction for future payment from property alleged to be held for its services.
The defendants challenged the suit’s maintainability but did not show how it was not maintainable.
issues.conclusion: The challenge to maintainability failed because no reason was shown why the suit could not be maintained.
issues.legal_principle: The Court rejected the objection because the appellants had not shown any basis for holding the suit not maintainable; no further statutory provision or earlier case was relied on for this point.

predicates.trustee_sues_for_endowment_income: A trustee brings a civil suit seeking income alleged to be held for a charitable endowment.
predicates.maintainability_defect_not_demonstrated: The party challenging the suit does not establish a reason why the suit cannot be maintained.

issues.definition: When a trustee sues for endowment income and the challenger establishes no maintainability defect, the maintainability objection fails.

issues.legal_issue: A plaint may be amended to add a formal prayer for relief when the relevant allegations and dispute were already pleaded and tried.
material_facts: The plaint contained allegations that the property was a specific endowment and that the defendants had failed to carry out its purpose, but did not include a formal prayer for a declaration.
The defendants raised the nature of the grant in their pleas, an issue was framed on that question, and both sides knew the points in controversy and led the necessary evidence.
The additional declaration was relief flowing from the existing allegations and did not require new facts or a fresh trial.
issues.conclusion: The High Court was right to allow the amendment adding the formal prayer for a declaration.
issues.legal_principle: An amendment adding formal relief may be allowed when necessary allegations have already been made, the parties have addressed the issue and led evidence, and the amendment does not change the cause of action or require a fresh trial.

rule.if: civil_suit_involving_endowment_claim and necessary_allegations_already_pleaded and parties_aware_of_dispute and necessary_evidence_led and added_prayer_is_formal_relief

predicates.civil_suit_involving_endowment_claim: A civil suit concerns whether property is held for an endowment and whether its purpose has been carried out.
predicates.necessary_allegations_already_pleaded: The plaint already alleges the material facts supporting the relief later sought.
predicates.parties_aware_of_dispute: The parties know the issue on which the additional relief depends, and it has been put in dispute.
predicates.necessary_evidence_led: The parties have already presented the evidence needed to decide that issue.
predicates.added_prayer_is_formal_relief: The added prayer follows from the existing allegations and does not require a new cause of action or a fresh trial.

issues.definition: If the endowment claim and its necessary factual basis were already disputed and tried, an amendment adding only formal relief may be allowed.

issues.legal_issue: A grant shown by the relevant records and surrounding evidence to be dedicated to a deity’s charitable service is a specific endowment rather than a personal grant burdened with a service obligation.
material_facts: An inam statement recorded that the present enjoyment was towards the deity’s festival service and that the income had been used for that service.
The inam register classified the grant as a religious endowment and recorded service at the temple; the sanad and title deed were not produced.
Predecessors of the defendants had acknowledged their role as trustees and their performance of the service.
Both lower courts found that the lands were endowed for the deity’s service and related purposes; the documentary evidence could support competing inferences.
issues.conclusion: The grant was a specific endowment constituting a specific trust, not a personal grant to the defendants subject to an obligation to spend on the service.
issues.legal_principle: Inam registers are evidence of utmost importance, particularly when the sanad and title deed are unavailable. The wording and context of the grant must be considered together; the distinction between confirmation so long as a service is performed and confirmation to a person so long as that person performs the service may indicate whether a grant is personal. Where the documents permit competing inferences, the Supreme Court will not interfere with the view taken below. The Court relied on Hindu Religious Endowments, Madras v. Thadikonda Koteswara Rao.

predicates.appeal_challenges_concurrent_grant_findi: An appeal challenges a finding by lower courts on whether a grant was dedicated to a charitable purpose or made personally subject to an obligation.
predicates.inam_records_indicate_charitable_purpose: The inam records describe the grant or its enjoyment as serving a religious or charitable purpose.
predicates.grantor_records_or_admissions_support_de: Other documentary evidence or relevant admissions support the conclusion that the property was dedicated to the stated purpose.

issues.definition: When an appeal challenges a concurrent finding and the records and related evidence support dedication to a charitable purpose, the grant is treated as a specific endowment.

issues.legal_issue: If the charitable payments specified when an endowment was created exhausted the property’s income, the whole income, including later increases or surplus, is devoted to the charity and may be applied cy-pres.
material_facts: At the time of the grant, the income was small and was entirely spent on the deity’s specified service.
The property’s income later exceeded the expenditure required for that service.
The High Court held that the whole income was for the deity and applied the cy-pres doctrine.
issues.conclusion: The whole income of the property was to go to the deity, including income exceeding the expenditure on the specified service.
issues.legal_principle: When specified charitable payments exhaust the income at the time of the grant, it is fair to infer an intention to devote the whole income to charity; later increases in the property’s value accrue to the charity. Where an endowment’s income is earmarked for its specified service and a surplus cannot be spent on that service, cy-pres may be applied. The Court relied on Hindu Religious Endowments v. Thadikonda Koteswara Rao, N. Sankaranarayana Pillayan v. The Board of Commissioners for Hindu Religious Endowments, Madras, Tudor on Charities, and Laws of England.

predicates.specific_charitable_endowment: Property is dedicated to a specific charitable or religious purpose.
predicates.original_income_exhausted_by_charitable_: At the time of the grant, the payments for the specified charitable purpose use the property’s entire income.
predicates.later_income_exceeds_service_needs: Later income is greater than the amount needed for the specified service.

issues.definition: If a specific charitable endowment originally uses all its income for its purpose and later income exceeds the service’s needs, the whole income remains devoted to charity.
